archetype: Explorer bow damage dealer built around a keydown main attack (Hurricane). Because the damage engine is a held-key channel rather than discrete casts, the class does not gain from the highest attack-speed brackets the way burst classes do, and its progression is unusually front-loaded onto a small number of 4th job skills (Hurricane, Final Attack, Arrow Blaster, Arrow Stream) that boost nodes and HEXA Mastery cores both target. Weapon multiplier 1.3x per Grandis Library. The class carries a large amount of Ignore DEF and Critical Rate from its own passives, which changes what it needs from gear and Inner Ability relative to other Explorers.

vMatrix.notes: The one thing every source agrees on is the shape rather than the exact trios: four nodes - Hurricane, Final Attack, Arrow Blaster, Arrow Stream - are taken to max before anything else, and everything below them is optional. That is the safe advice to give a player. Exact trio pairings are the weakest part of the public Bow Master record: the class doc encodes them in images, Grandis Library only publishes Primary/Secondary/Other buckets rather than pairings, and the only explicit written trios come from a source whose data is stated as 2024-05-14 and therefore predates the v269 boost-node grouping changes that Grandis Library's own 'View Pre-V.269 Boost Nodes' toggle is evidence of. Do not present trio pairings with the same confidence as the mandatory four.

order.step: Ascendant Shadow (Origin skill) - unlock and take to Lv. 1 immediately
order.why: The Origin skill is the first HEXA node and the single largest damage addition available at 6th job. The class doc also records it as a defensive tool: roughly a 4.5 second invincibility window during its cutscene, on a 6 minute cooldown, which makes it a rotation anchor rather than just a damage button. It gains extra innate stats at Lv. 10, 20 and 30.

Second HEXA node. The class doc describes three uses per boss fight (six key presses), or a 4 minute cooldown outside boss content. Like the Origin skill it gains additional innate stats at Lv. 10, 20 and 30.
Hurricane is the keydown main attack, so its Mastery core upgrades the skill that delivers most of the class's damage in every situation. The class doc puts it at the head of the Mastery order.

order.step: Mastery cores: Arrow Stream VI and Arrow Blaster VI
order.why: Second group in the class doc's Mastery order. The doc does not rank these two against each other; a training-focused character leans Arrow Stream, a bossing one Arrow Blaster, which follows from the same skills' roles in the boost node section.

order.step: Common cores: Sol Janus to Lv. 1 early; Fury of the Wild VI; Sol Hecate to Lv. 1, then 20, then 30
order.why: Sol Janus at Lv. 1 is called out as an early farming pickup, with further levels dependent on how much the character farms. The class doc says Fury of the Wild VI costs less in both Fragments and Sol Erda than the other Common skills, which is a cost-efficiency argument for taking it earlier. Sol Hecate's value is gated on breakpoints: the summon and Styx at Lv. 1, Charon (a death-prevention effect) at Lv. 20, and Phlegethon at Lv. 30, so partial investment between those levels buys little.

order.step: HEXA Stat: prioritise ATT, then DEX, then Boss Damage
order.why: Stated directly by the class doc as ATT > DEX > Boss%. The doc adds the practical point that rolls should be rearranged so the largest value sits on the highest-priority line, rather than assuming attack always belongs in the main line.

hexa.notes: IMPORTANT STRUCTURAL FACT, and the most product-relevant thing in this file: the class doc does not publish a single flat HEXA order. It publishes separate charts chosen along two axes. Axis one is server type - Heroic/Reboot players are told to use the FRAGMENT LIMITED charts, Interactive players the ENERGY LIMITED charts, because the two worlds bottleneck on different currencies. Axis two is what the character is for, with three variants: Main/Min-Clear, Legion Champ, and Mule/Culvert. Grandis Library independently publishes three 6th Job infographics under those same three names, which corroborates the three-way split even though Grandis credits the class doc for its build content. A planner that emits one universal Bow Master HEXA order is therefore contradicting the class's own maintained guide. The detailed step-by-step sequences live inside those images and did not survive text extraction, so the per-step target levels are NOT recorded here - only the category order above, which came from the doc's prose. Anyone completing this file should read the infographics directly. Secondary claim, weak and unverified: the class doc states Mastery cores require the relevant V matrix boost nodes at Lv. 40+ and Enhancement nodes require Lv. 25+ job nodes; those thresholds came through text extraction and were not cross-checked against the wiki's HEXA mechanics page, so confirm in game before relying on them.

priority.stat: Critical Rate - roughly 7 to 10 points, late game, ON TOP of reaching 100%
priority.why: This is the Bow Master-specific one and the reason a generic hyper stat list is wrong for this class. Vicious Shot lets Critical Rate exceed the 100% cap and converts total Critical Rate into Critical Damage at a 50% ratio, so crit rate keeps scaling damage after the point where every other class stops buying it. The class doc recommends carrying roughly 7-10 extra points of Critical Rate in hyper stats once the relevant node is maxed. Grandis Library independently lists Vicious Shot's effect as granting 50% of Critical Rate, which corroborates the mechanic even though it does not state the hyper stat recommendation.

hyperStats.notes: The class doc explicitly declines to publish a fixed hyper stat order, on the grounds that the optimal allocation depends on the character's own stat sheet, and points readers at a calculator instead. That refusal is itself the finding and should be surfaced to users rather than papered over with a static list: the community's operative answer to hyper stat priority is MathBro's per-character optimizer, not a ranking. The ordering above should be presented as a starting shape, with the Critical Rate overflow point as the class-specific rule that a generic optimizer preset will get wrong if it caps crit at 100%.

innerAbility.notes: The attack speed +1 line, which is a standard recommendation for Explorer classes, is NOT wanted here. The class doc states Bow Master is a keydown class that does not benefit from the top attack speed bracket and naturally reaches its useful cap from gear. This matches the cross-class rule recorded on the community wiki's Inner Ability guide, which scopes the attack speed line to Explorer classes that lack a Hurricane-type skill - Bow Master is the class that rule is carving out. That is an independent lane agreeing with the class doc, which is why this is the best-supported Inner Ability claim in the file. Both Inner Ability presets themselves are one consensus family (Grandis Library credits 'Class Doc' for its Inner Ability section), hence weak.

gearingNotes:
Bow Master changes gearing advice in four specific ways, all sourced to the class doc unless noted.

1. CRITICAL RATE DOES NOT STOP AT 100%. Vicious Shot allows Critical Rate to exceed the cap and converts total Critical Rate into Critical Damage at a 50% ratio. Grandis Library independently lists the skill as granting 50% of Critical Rate. Practical consequence: keep buying crit rate past the point where other classes stop - the class doc suggests roughly 7-10 extra hyper stat points late game - and do not let a planner or optimizer hard-cap crit at 100% for this class.

2. NO IED LINES ON WEAPON, SECONDARY OR EMBLEM. The class doc states Bow Master's own passives already supply enough Ignore DEF that IED lines on WSE are not needed, and recommends a 9/0/0 attack/boss/IED main potential loadout instead. The two sources disagree on how much IED the passives actually give - the class doc cites two passives contributing 40% and 25%, while Grandis Library's base-stats-from-skills summary totals 59.85% Ignore DEF - so the exact number is contested, but both agree it is large.

3. NO COOLDOWN HAT. The class doc says to stack %DEX on the hat rather than taking a cooldown-reduction hat. This is a real fork for players coming from classes where the cooldown hat is standard.

4. ATTACK SPEED CAPS EARLY. As a keydown class it does not benefit from the highest attack speed bracket; the class doc puts the useful natural cap at 8 from gear. This removes the attack speed inner ability line and de-prioritises attack speed sources generally.

Other sourced gearing facts from the class doc: Titanium Arrows give +9 attack and only a single arrow needs to be held in the inventory; Blood Arrows cost roughly 4% damage relative to Magic Arrows and should only be used when the sustain is actually needed; Ring of Restraint and Continuous Ring are both kept equipped; the Legion grid is ranked Critical Damage > Boss Damage > IED = Critical Rate > DEX > ATT > Buff Duration. The class doc also names an endgame secondary weapon and emblem, but those item names could not be validated against a skill/item table in this session and are deliberately omitted rather than risk printing a wrong item name.

contest.method: An independent agent re-searched every claim in this file without seeing the researcher's reasoning, and was instructed to refute rather than confirm.
defects: The merged node entry 'Final Attack (class doc writes Advanced Final Attack; Grandis Library writes Final Attack: Bow)' and the matching conflict entry 'Three sources, three strings, one node' assert an identity that no source states, and Grandis contradicts it. Grandis's skill table lists Final Attack: Bow (2nd Job) AND Advanced Final Attack (4th Job) as two separate, co-existing skills. Grandis's Node 1 boosts Final Attack: Bow; the class doc's mandatory four names Advanced Final Attack. That is a possible real disagreement about which skill the node targets, collapsed into an alias problem. boostNodeTargets then ships only 'Final Attack: Bow', so downstream code would emit the 2nd job name under guide text that says Advanced Final Attack.

archetype: 'its progression is unusually front-loaded onto a small number of 4th job skills (Hurricane, Final Attack, Arrow Blaster, Arrow Stream) that boost nodes and HEXA Mastery cores both target.' Per Grandis's skill table only two of those four are 4th job. Arrow Blaster is 3rd Job and Final Attack: Bow is 2nd Job. The claim that HEXA Mastery cores and boost nodes target the same set is asserted with no source and is doubtful for a 3rd job skill.

conflicts, bossing trio entry: the reasoning 'Erda Nova is a 5th job skill and boost nodes target 4th job skills' rests on a false premise. Grandis's node list contains 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th and Hyper skills (Gritty Gust is explicitly labelled Hyper Skill). The conclusion is probably still right, but the stated reason is invented.

'Extra Quiver Cartridge' (hexa.order group 3 and skillNameReference.hexaMastery) appears in no source I could reach. It is absent from Grandis's full skill table, which instead lists a 4th job skill 'Enchanted Quiver'. Given it came from text extraction of an image-heavy document, treat it as a probable extraction artifact until a second source shows it. skillNameReference claims 'Every name here appears literally in at least one source listed; none are inferred' - that claim is only as strong as the extraction.

'Flashpoint' as the Ascent skill is single-sourced to the same text extraction. Grandis's 6th Job section lists only Ascendant Shadow. Absence is not disconfirmation (Grandis is at v269 and Ascent skills may postdate it), but hexa.order presents it flatly as 'Second HEXA node' with no second source anywhere. 'Ascendant Shadow' by contrast IS independently confirmed by Grandis.

hyperStats.priority is an ordered array reading Critical Damage > IED > Boss Damage > Damage, and the Critical Damage entry justifies first place with 'the class doc also ranks Critical Damage first on the Legion grid'. The class doc calls these an unordered 'big 4' and explicitly declines to rank hyper stats; the Legion grid is a different system. The file's own notes admit the doc refuses to order, then ships an ordered array anyway - downstream code will read array position as priority.
